mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with declines in FEDFUNDS during periods of monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns following a 0.2pp increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in unemployment and decreases in payroll employment indicate labor market distress, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns despite concurrent increases in UNRATE and decreases in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply-side weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns following a 1 point decrease in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate may indicate tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Increases in housing starts and consumer spending suggest strong demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns despite increases in HOUST and RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-interest-rate environment, inflation (as measured by CPI) may lead to higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns during periods of low interest rates and rising CPI.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns following payroll employment growth.
